bodyHtml:
A decision guide to React: what it is for, when it fits, how to start, and which compatibility or maintenance details deserve a closer look.

Quick verdict

React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces.

Shortlist React only if its documented purpose matches your use case; the source signals below are context, not an endorsement.

Best fit — and when to skip it

React is most relevant to developers working with JavaScript/TypeScript. Its source topics point to react. It belongs on a shortlist when that stated purpose matches a concrete requirement.

Skip or postpone it when the documented runtime, license, dependency footprint, or maintenance model conflicts with your project. Popularity alone is not a reason to migrate.

Setup and first checks

Confirm the exact package name, current version, runtime requirement, dependencies, provenance, and release notes before installing react in a production project. Start in a disposable example and exercise the use case you actually need.

Maintenance and risk signals

The collected source record shows 161.3M weekly downloads, version 19.2.8, and released 2026-07-21.

The recorded Node.js requirement is >=0.10.0.

The registry lists 2 maintainers.

The source reports the MIT license.

Registry downloads include automated requests and are not unique users, satisfaction, or proof of quality.

Bottom line

React is worth a closer look when its stated purpose and ecosystem fit your project. Compare it with related tools, verify the current documentation, and test the smallest realistic use case before committing.

Try it safely

npm install react

Use the official npm package page to confirm the current version, documentation, dependencies, provenance, and compatibility requirements before installing it in an important project.
